faqs.question: What should be the monthly pension under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary will receive a sum of [?]1500/-, [?] 2,000/- & [?]2500/- as monthly pension under this scheme as per their eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: How long will a beneficiary receive a monthly pension under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The beneficiary will get a pension as long as he/she is alive.

faqs.question: What is the age limit under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant should have attained the age of 60 years.

faqs.question: Is this scheme applicable for both husband & wife?
faqs.answer: In case both the husband & wife are old age persons and are eligible for Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), only one member of the family shall be awarded the pension. In case of death of the pensioner, such pension shall be transferred to his/her spouse, if alive on surrender of the pass book, provided he/she has attained the age of 60 (sixty) years of age or more.

faqs.question: Is this scheme applicable only for Below Poverty Line (BPL) category?
faqs.answer: Yes, only a member of the BPL family of Sikkim state is eligible under the scheme.

faqs.question: Is a person drawing any other pension under Central / State Government or from any other sources eligible under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, any person drawing any other pension under Central / State Government or from any other sources is not eligible for the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the mode of filling application?
faqs.answer: The applicant may fill application both online & offline mode.

faqs.question: How can I register under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Please visit the online portal link: https://pensionscheme.sikkim.gov.in and use the "Create Account" button to reach the registration page. Complete registration requirements as appropriate and click the "Register" button to register and then login.

faqs.question: How will the pension distributed under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The pension shall be distributed through Direct Benefit Transfer System or any other system as may be decided by the Sanctioning / Competent Authority from time to time.

faqs.question: Should I need to submit "Life Certificate" every year?
faqs.answer: Yes, each beneficiary of the Pensions should submit a "Life Certificate" in the prescribed format in the month of November every year failing which it will be presumed that the beneficiary is either died or migrated outside the State of Sikkim and the payment of pension shall be stopped forthwith without further notice.

ignwps.briefDescription: A non-contributory pension scheme to provide social security to widows of poor family (BPL)  of the society.
ignwps.detailedDescription: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) is implemented by Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India. It is a non-contributory pension scheme to provide social security to widows of poor family (BPL)  of the society.
ignwps.benefits: A pension of ₹ 300/- per month is provided to Widows between 40 years and 79 years. For persons who are 80 years and above, the pension is ₹ 500/- per month.

faqs.question: What pension amount is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible beneficiaries receive Central Assistance of ₹300 per month. Beneficiaries aged 80 years and above receive ₹500 per month.

faqs.question: Is there any income criterion for availing the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. The applicant must belong to a household identified as living Below Poverty Line (BPL) as per the criteria prescribed by the Government of India.

faqs.question: Can a widow above 80 years continue receiving benefits?

faqs.answer: Applications can be submitted through the prescribed process followed by the concerned State Government, Gram Panchayat, Municipality, or designated welfare authority.

faqs.question: Can a widow receive benefits from both Central and State pension schemes?

faqs.question: What is the objective of the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to provide financial security and social assistance to destitute widows from economically vulnerable households, helping them meet their basic needs and live with dignity.

faqs.question: What is the IGNDPS?
faqs.answer: The IGNDPS is a component of the National Social Assistance Programme that provides monthly financial assistance to persons with severe or multiple disabilities belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.

faqs.question: Which ministry implements the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under IGNDPS?
faqs.answer: The person with severe or multiple disabilities must be aged 18 and above and belong to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) household as per government norms.

faqs.question: What is the benefit provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Eligible beneficiaries receive a monthly pension under the scheme. The central government provides financial assistance.

faqs.question: What type of disability is covered under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme covers persons with severe or multiple disabilities as defined under applicable government guidelines and disability certification norms.

faqs.question: Is a disability certificate mandatory for applying?
faqs.answer: Yes. The applicant must possess a valid disability certificate issued by a competent medical authority or medical board.

faqs.question: Can a beneficiary receive pension from another social welfare pension scheme simultaneously?
faqs.answer: No. Generally, a beneficiary receiving another social welfare pension is not eligible to receive benefits under the same category of pension schemes.

faqs.question: How can one apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants can apply through the UMANG platform, NSAP portal, or through the concerned State/UT authorities and local bodies as prescribed by the respective state government.

faqs.question: When was the IGNDPS launched?
faqs.answer: The Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) was formally launched in February 2009 under the National Social Assistance Programme.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available in both rural and urban areas?
faqs.answer: Yes. The National Social Assistance Programme, including IGNDPS, is implemented in both rural and urban areas across India.

rvy.briefDescription: The scheme encourages citizens to help road accident victims during emergencies by providing a ₹25,000 incentive to individuals who save lives through timely medical assistance.
rvy.detailedDescription: The “Raah-Veer Yojana” was launched by the Home Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh. It aims to encourage the general public to help road accident victims during emergencies and save innocent lives during the critical Golden Hour by rewarding citizens who voluntarily take accident victims to a hospital for treatment. The scheme promotes civic responsibility and compassion among citizens by recognizing their bravery and humanitarian actions. > **Scheme Implementation** It is implemented by the Office of the Transport Commissioner, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, under the supervision of the State and District-Level Evaluation Committees and monitored by the Home Department.
rvy.benefits: **Tangible Benefits** - Provides a cash reward of ₹25,000 to individuals (“Rah-Veers”) who save the life of an accident victim by taking them to a hospital within the Golden Hour. - Selected “Rah-Veers” may be nominated for national-level awards by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH). - The MoRTH Evaluation Committee selects the top 10 Rah-Veers nationwide, each awarded ₹1,00,000, a certificate, and a trophy at the National Road Safety Mission (NRSM) in New Delhi. - Each individual can be awarded a maximum of 5 times per year under this scheme. **Mode of Disbursement** - The payment is made online directly to the beneficiary’s bank account through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). **Frequency of Disbursement** - One-time per eligible instance, up to a maximum of 5 instances per year. **Expected Time of Disbursement** - The payment is processed within 1 month after the District Evaluation Committee’s approval.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md: 1. The applicant should be a resident of Madhya Pradesh. 1. The applicant should be any individual (citizen or resident) who voluntarily assists a road accident victim in a motor vehicle-related accident. 1. The applicant must have helped the victim reach a hospital within the Golden Hour, ensuring the victim’s survival.

children.text: The applicant should be a resident of Madhya Pradesh.
The applicant should be any individual (citizen or resident) who voluntarily assists a road accident victim in a motor vehicle-related accident.
The applicant must have helped the victim reach a hospital within the Golden Hour, ensuring the victim’s survival.
Incident Reporting by the Applicant:

The Rah-Veer informs the police first, the police will verify details with the attending doctor and issue an official acknowledgment slip containing the Rah-Veer’s name, mobile number, address, location, date, time, and details of assistance.
A copy of this slip is sent to the District Evaluation Committee and one to the Rah-Veer.
Direct Hospital Assistance:
If the Rah-Veer takes the victim directly to the hospital, the hospital must inform the local police station.
The police then issue the acknowledgment slip as above.
District-Level Evaluation Committee:
Composed of the District Magistrate, Superintendent of Police (SSP), Chief Medical Officer (CMOH), and Regional Transport Officer (RTO).
Reviews and approves the cases on a monthly basis.
State-Level Monitoring:
Headed by the Principal Secretary (Home) with members including the Commissioner (Health), ADGP (Traffic and Road Safety), and Commissioner (Transport) as Member Secretary.
Conducts quarterly reviews to ensure smooth implementation.
Disbursement:
After approval, the Transport Commissioner, Bhopal, processes the payment directly into the Rah-Veer’s bank account through PFMS.
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) provides monthly reimbursement to the State Transport Department.
National-Level Recognition:
Each year, up to three exceptional Rah-Veers are nominated for national awards.

faqs.answer: Any individual who saves an accident victim by providing timely medical help.

faqs.question: What is the reward amount?
faqs.answer: ₹25,000 per recognized act of assistance.

faqs.question: How many times can a person receive the award in a year?
faqs.answer: A person receives the award up to 5 times per year.

faqs.question: What is the “Golden Hour”?
faqs.answer: The first hour after a road accident when prompt medical aid can save a victim’s life.

faqs.question: How can someone apply for recognition?
faqs.answer: Through police verification and submission of acknowledgment and hospital reports.

faqs.answer: The District Evaluation Committee forwards approved names to the Transport Commissioner.

faqs.question: How is the payment made?
faqs.answer: Through online transfer via the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).

faqs.question: Is there any application fee?
faqs.answer: No, the process is completely free.

faqs.question: Can the Rah-Veer remain anonymous?
faqs.answer: No, anonymous individuals cannot receive the award.

faqs.question: Can Rah-Veers be nominated for national awards?
faqs.answer: Yes, up to 3 Rah-Veers from each state can be nominated for national-level recognition.

pmuy.briefDescription: A scheme by Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas for Providing free LPG connections to women belonging to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.
pmuy.detailedDescription:
In May 2016, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MOPNG), introduced the ‘Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana’ (PMUY) as a flagship scheme with an objective to make clean cooking fuel such as LPG available to the rural and deprived households which were otherwise using traditional cooking fuels such as firewood, coal, cow-dung cakes etc. Usage of traditional cooking fuels had detrimental impacts on the health of rural women as well as on the environment.
The scheme was launched on 1st May 2016 in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri. Narendra Modi


- The target under the scheme was to release 8 Crore LPG Connections to the deprived households by March 2020.
- On 7th September 2019, Hon’ble Prime Minister of India handed over the 8th Crore LPG connection in Aurangabad, Maharashtra.
- The release of 8 Crore LPG connections under the scheme has also helped in increasing the LPG coverage from 62% on 1st May 2016 to 99.8% as on 1st April 2021.
- Under the Union Budget for FY 21-22, provision for release of additional 1 Crore LPG connections under the PMUY scheme has been made. In this phase, special facility has been given to migrant families.
pmuy.benefits:
1. Rs. 1600 for a connection 14.2kg cylinder or Rs. 1150 for a 5 kg cylinder. 1. Additionally, All PMUY beneficiaries will be provided with first LPG refill and Stove (hot plate) both free of cost along with their deposit free connection.
#### Note: Priority would be given to the states which have lower LPG coverage (Compared to the national average) as on 1st Jan 2016.
pmuy.exclusions: Male Member from a household cannot apply for the scheme.

1. If she is not falling in the above 2 categories, then she can stake her claim to be a beneficiary under Poor household by submitting 14-point declaration (as per prescribed format)

faqs.question: What is the objective of the “Working Women Hostel” scheme?
faqs.answer: The objective of the “Working Women Hostel” scheme is to provide safe, secure, and affordable residential facilities to employed women, especially those who have migrated for work and need reliable accommodation near their place of employment.

faqs.question: Which department is responsible for implementing the “Working Women Hostel” scheme in Haryana?
faqs.answer: The Women and Child Development Department, Government of Haryana, is responsible for the implementation and overall supervision of the “Working Women Hostel” scheme across various designated locations in the state.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme?
faqs.answer: Any woman who is currently working and requires accommodation due to employment away from her native residence is eligible to apply under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme.

faqs.question: What are the rent charges applicable to beneficiaries staying in hostels under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme, the rent charged from beneficiaries is subsidized and varies depending on the type of room; it is limited to 15% of gross salary for single bedrooms, 10% for double bedrooms, and 7.5% for dormitory accommodation.

faqs.question: Are there any income limits or salary caps for availing hostel accommodation?
faqs.answer: Although the scheme does not specify a strict income cap, the rent charged is proportionate to the applicant’s salary, thereby making the accommodation affordable for working women across different income brackets.

faqs.question: What is the process for applying to the "Working Women Hostel" scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicants may visit the [Antyodaya-SARAL Portal](https://saralharyana.gov.in/) to apply for the scheme.

faqs.question: What is the offline process for applying the scheme?
faqs.answer: To apply for the "Working Women Hostel" scheme, the applicant may visit the nearest Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre).

faqs.question: Is there any fee applicable for applying under this scheme through Atal Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre)?
faqs.answer: Yes, a nominal service fee of ₹10/- is charged by the Common Service Centre for the application.

faqs.question: Are there any specific documents that need to be submitted with the application form?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants are required to submit several documents, including the Parivar Pehchan Patra Number, visitor list, local guardian appointment and acceptance, medical certificate, undertaking, character certificate, and a financial guarantee.

faqs.question: Does the scheme provide hostel facilities in all districts of Haryana?
faqs.answer: Yes, hostel facilities under the “Working Women Hostel” scheme is provided in all districts of Haryana.

pmsgmb.briefDescription: "PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana" is a government scheme that aims to provide free electricity to households in India.
pmsgmb.detailedDescription: "PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana" is a government scheme that aims to provide free electricity to households in India. The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on February 15, 2024. Under the scheme, households will be provided with a subsidy to install solar panels on their roofs. The subsidy will cover up to 40% of the cost of the solar panels. The scheme is expected to benefit 1 crore households across India. It is estimated that the scheme will save the government Rs. 75,000 crore per year in electricity costs.

faqs.question: What types of roofs are suitable for Rooftop solar (RTS) system?
faqs.answer: Rooftop solar PV systems can be installed on any type of roof having sufficient load bearing capacity.

faqs.question: What are the advantages of Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar System?
faqs.answer:
Saving on electricity bill by the consumer.
Utilization of available vacant roof space, no additional land required.
Low gestation period.
No additional requirement of transmission and distribution (T&D) lines.
Reduces T&D losses as power consumption and generation are collocated.
Improvement in the tail-end grid voltages and reduction of system congestion.
Long term energy and ecological security by reduction in carbon emission.
Better management of daytime peak loads by DISCOM/ utility.
Meeting of the Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs) of obligated entities

faqs.question: Can applicant install Rooftop Solar system if applicant live in a rented house?

The RTS under any framework like net or gross metering can be installed by the electricity consumer. So, if applicant have electricity connection in his/her name and he/she pay regularly the electricity bill in his/her own name and also have the permission of use
the roof for solar rooftop installation from the owner, he/she can install the RTS.

faqs.question: If applicant shift his/her residence or office where RTS is installed, what will happen to the RTS?
faqs.answer: The system is easy to be dismantled and reassembled elsewhere. So, it can be shifted to new residence.

jjm.briefDescription: Jal Jeevan Mission, is envisioned to provide safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections by 2024 to all households in rural India.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md: This scheme is applicable to all households in rural India.

children.text: This scheme is applicable to all households in rural India.
The applicant need not apply for the scheme.

State Governments/ UT Administration will implement the mission based on the finalized SAP with timelines to cover all the villages of the respective State/ UT. Each village will be assessed on existing water supply infrastructure by DWSM in consultation with Gram Panchayat and/ or its sub-committee and ISA. Based on the same, FHTCs will be provided to every rural household by creating in-village water supply infrastructure including source development under any one of the following suggested categories, viz.
Retrofitting of ongoing schemes taken up under erstwhile NRDWP for the last mile connectivity;
Retrofitting of completed rural water supply schemes to make it JJM compliant;
Single Village Scheme (SVS) in villages having adequate groundwater/ spring water/ local or surface water source of prescribed quality;
Single Village Scheme (SVS) in villages having adequate groundwater that needs treatment;
Multi Village Scheme (MVS) with water grids/ regional water supply scheme; and
Mini solar power-based piped water supply in isolated/ tribal hamlets.

documents: Any proof of identity like Voter ID / Passport / Driving License / Ration Card / Aadhaar Card etc. is sufficient to apply for water connection

faqs.question: How water will be provided to households where tap water connections are not feasible?
faqs.answer:
In such areas, local innovations/ technological solutions will be explored. Suggestive technological solutions to address challenges in the supply of drinking water are as under:

Solar energy based stand-alone water supply systems for scattered/ isolated/ tribal/ hilly villages.
Community Water Purification Plant (CWPP) in groundwater contaminated areas.
In cold deserts, solutions may be explored to enhance and store run-off water in small tanks - traditional water harvesting structure, i.e. Zings of Ladakh. Further, artificial glacial reservoirs may be created by diverting the run-off to freeze & store as glacier.
In hard rock areas, bore-blast technique, fracture seal cementation, stream blasting, etc. may be explored.
In hilly areas, adopting spring-based sources, rain water harvesting and standalone bore-well systems (if feasible) will be explored.
In coastal areas, energy efficient small desalination plants with high recovery ratio will be explored, along with construction of sub-surface dykes in rivers.
Use of Internet of Things (IoT), Geographic Information System (GIS) software, etc., will be required for planning and monitoring.

mdiis.briefDescription: An opportunity for a student to secure practical work experience under the guidance of a qualified and experienced Supervisor/Mentor in Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) in the form of Digital India Internship Scheme.
mdiis.detailedDescription:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has introduced an internship scheme named &quot;**Digital India Internship Scheme**.&quot; It aims to offer practical exposure and professional experience to students pursuing graduate or postgraduate degrees in technology, engineering, or management. Interns get the opportunity to work on live projects related to the Digital India initiative, enabling them to understand the functioning of e-Governance and contribute to ongoing digital transformation efforts.
***Scheme Implement:***
The scheme is implemented by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), a part of MeitY. 
***Duration of Internship:***
The minimum duration of the internship shall be two months, extendable up to three months, depending on the performance of the candidate and the requirements of the ministry.
***Areas of Internship:***
There are a total of 29 slots available for the internship in 23 different types of areas ([Annexure](https://intern.meity.gov.in/public/assets/Files/DIIS-2025.pdf)). 
***Place of Internship:***
The internship will be offered at New Delhi.
mdiis.benefits:
1. A token stipend of ₹10,000/- per month would be paid to an intern, subject to satisfactory performance, duly certified by his supervisor/mentor.
   1. Certificates will be issued by the Ministry to the interns upon the completion of the internship and submission of the Report duly countersigned and accepted by the competent authority.

<br>

> **NOTE:**



    - The intern shall be paid after the completion of the internship on submission of a report duly accepted by this ministry.
mdiis.exclusions:
1. The internship is neither employment nor an assurance of employment with the ministry. 
   1. The students who are in the last semester or who will pass out in summer 2025 will not be eligible for the internship.
   1. Possessing minimum qualifications as above shall not guarantee an internship in this ministry. 
   1. No TA/DA shall be paid to candidates for attending the personal interview. 
   1. The intern shall not claim any intellectual property rights for work done at the ministry and has to strictly maintain the confidentiality of the ministry’s intellectual property. 
   1. An intern may not interact with or represent the ministry vis-à-vis third parties. However, some Interns may specifically be authorized to interact with third parties on behalf of the Ministry depending on the nature of their roles and responsibilities. 
   1. No intern shall interact with or represent the ministry to the media (print and electronic).

faqs.question: How are interns selected?

faqs.question: Does this internship guarantee a job in MeitY?

faqs.question: What happens if an intern performs unsatisfactorily?

faqs.question: Is preference given to students from certain academic fields?

pmgsy.briefDescription: With the objective of providing rural connectivity, the Government of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (referred to as PMGSY-I hereinafter) on 25th December 2000 to provide all-weather access to eligible unconnected habitations.
pmgsy.detailedDescription:
With the objective of providing rural connectivity, the Government of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (referred to as PMGSY-I hereinafter) on 25th December 2000 to provide all-weather access to eligible unconnected habitations with a population of up to 500(Census 2001) in plain area and 250 and above in Special category States(States of North East, Jammu, and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand), Desert Area as identified by Desert Development Program and 88 selected Backward Districts as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs/Planning Commission as a strategy for poverty alleviation.
As of 8th December 2021, a total of 6,80,040 km of road length has been constructed under various interventions of Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY). The primary objective of PMGSY concerns building robust, all-weather roads in rural habitations and other core areas. Panchayati Rajs and elected local representatives decide which habitations to be selected. This scheme was centrally funded only up to 2015-16. Since then, the funds have been divided between the Centre and the State. For North Eastern and Himalayan States (Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh) 90% of a project is the Union Government funds, and 10% of this cost, is the State Government funds. For the Other States, the Union Government funds around 60% of a project while the remaining 40% is by State Government funds.
Some prominent features of PMGSY are - Proper decentralized planning for the building of roads. Build roads according to the Indian Road Congress and Rural Roads Manual. 3-tier quality management system. An unbroken flow of funds.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md:
1. A region must be a habitation. It cannot be a hamlet or revenue village to be eligible for the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY).
2. The Central Government describes habitation as a population cluster residing within an area that remains constant over time. Some of the local words used to describe a habitation are: Majras, Desam, Hamlets, Tolas, Dhanis
3. The hamlet must have a higher population as per the 2001 Census to be eligible for road connection. The eligible habitations have a population of above 500 persons in plain areas and around 250 persons and above in hilly areas.

The list of road works to be taken up under the Programme will be finalized each year by the District Panchayat in accordance with the allocation of funds communicated to the district. The District Panchayat has to ensure along with the consultative process, that the lists of proposed road works are part of the Core Network and that new connectivity is given priority.

faqs.question: Does The Programme Provide Connectivity To Only Revenue Villages? Are Hamlets Eligible To Be Connected?
faqs.answer:
The spirit and objective of PMGSY-I was to provide good all-weather road connectivity to eligible unconnected habitations. The unit of this programme is a habitation and not a revenue village or a Panchayat. A habitation is a cluster of population, living in an area, the location of which does not change over time. Desam, Dhanis, Tolas, Majras, Hamlets, etc. are commonly used to describe habitations.

The population, as recorded in the Census 2001, shall be the basis for determining the population size of the habitation. The population of all Habitations within a radius of 500 metre (1.5 km of path distance in case of Hills) may be clubbed together to determine the population size. In the blocks bordering international boundary in the hill States (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs), however, all habitations within a path distance of 10 km may be treated as a cluster for this purpose. This cluster approach would enable the provision of connectivity to a number of Habitations, particularly in Hill/ mountainous areas.

A special dispensation has been allowed to Arunachal Pradesh under PMGSY by extending the Cluster approach to all International border districts in the State by clubbing population with the path distance of 10 km and treating as a Cluster.

faqs.question: How Are Habitations Selected For Coverage? Who Decides Which Habitations Will Be Covered In A Year?
faqs.answer: Unconnected habitations are listed as per the priority (generally, habitations with a higher population, as per 2001 Census, would be connected first) and depending upon the funds likely to be made available for the State, the list of road works to be taken up under PMGSY-I will be finalized each year by the District Panchayat through a consultative process involving Panchayati Raj Institutions and elected representatives.

faqs.question: Can An Individual Apply For Road Connectivity?
faqs.answer: The objective of PMGSY-I was to provide road connectivity to unconnected habitations as mentioned in response to Question 1 above. Any proposal for road connectivity may be perceived as per the programme guidelines.

faqs.question: How Is Alignment Selected? Are Local Villagers Associated With This Process?
faqs.answer: A simple, non-formal transect walk shall be organised by the Assistant Engineer at the time of preparation of DPRs to finalise the alignment. The Panchayat Pradhan, local patwari, the JE, Local Revenue and Forest officials, Women PRI members and representatives of Women Self Help Groups (SHGs) also participate in the transect walk to determine the most suitable alignment, sort out the issues of land availability and to moderate any adverse social and environmental impact, eliciting necessary community participation in the programme. After transect walk, the minutes should be placed and approved by the Grama Sabha.Local people including those likely to be affected by proposed alignment are also allowed to put forth their view in this process.

faqs.question: What Does All-Weather Connectivity Mean? Does It Mean Only Black- Topped Or Cement Concrete Roads?
faqs.answer: An all-weather road is one that is negotiable in all seasons of the year. This implies that the road-bed is drained effectively but this does not necessarily imply that it should be paved surface with blacktopping or cement concrete. A gravel road can also be an all-weather road.

faqs.question: How Is The Problem Of Drainage Tackled In The Portion Of Roads Passing Through Built-Up Residential Areas?
faqs.answer: Road portions passing through built-up residential areas are prone to damages caused by wastewater from households. Programme guidelines provide for the construction of cement concrete pavement or cement/stone block pavements along with covered or uncovered Pucca side drains as per site conditions.

faqs.question: Is The Adequate Provision For Culverts Or Cross-Drainage Works Made?
faqs.answer:
The objective of the PMGSY is to provide an All-weather Road with necessary culverts and other cross drainage structures, which is operable throughout the year to the eligible unconnected habitations as per PMGSY guidelines in the rural areas. Rural roads constructed under PMGSY must have proper embankment and drainage. Adequate number and type of Cross Drainage (CD) works, including causeways, where appropriate, must be provided based on site requirements ascertained through necessary investigation. Minor bridges can be provided wherever necessary.

A necessary advisory has been already issued to the State Governments to include the culverts/CDs bridges along with the road proposals.

The proposal of long-span Bridges should be prepared as a separate DPR. However, such proposals of Bridges should be submitted with road proposals in the same batch.

faqs.question: What About Bridges On Rivers/Streams?
faqs.answer:
Bridges on rivers/streams crossing the alignment of the road are taken up under the program along with the road proposal. The Ministry issued PMGSY-III guidelines increasing the span of Long-Span Bridges (LSBs) for funding under PMGSY as follows:

Up to 200 m in respect of Special Category States and LWE districts identified by the MHA.
Upto 150 m in respect of other States.

faqs.question: Whether Compensation For Land Acquisition Is Paid In The Program?
faqs.answer: The rural road is a State subject and it is the responsibility of State Government/ District Panchayat to ensure the availability of land for construction of road works under the programme. In view of the common benefit, generally, the land for construction of roads under PMGSY is made available by the villagers/Panchayat free of cost through voluntary donation. However, in rare cases, if the land is acquired for construction of roads under PMGSY, the State Government is required to pay compensation.

faqs.question: How Are Executants Selected For The Construction Of Roads?
faqs.answer: Executants for construction of roads are selected through open competitive bidding for which well-established procedure for tendering is followed by the State Government. As per provisions, the bidders who have the prescribed qualifications and have the capacity to execute the works are required to take part in the bidding process. To enhance the transparency in tendering and speed up the tendering process, e- procurement of bids has been made mandatory.

faqs.question: If Defects Are Noticed After Completion Of The Road, How Are They Rectified?
faqs.answer: As per provisions of the contract, the contractor is liable for any defect that may occur until 5 years after completion of the road work. To enforce liability of defects, the security amount is deducted from the bills of the contractors. The contractor has to rectify the defect in the above period and if the rectification has not been carried out, the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) is required to rectify the defect and recover the cost from the security deposit of the contractor.

faqs.question: How Is The Quality Of Work Checked And Monitored?
faqs.answer: Every contractor is required to establish a field laboratory in every package of road works in which he/she required to test the quality of material and workmanship under the supervision of executing agency. In addition to checking of quality by departmental officers of executing agency, the State Government is required to deploy independent monitors for monitoring of the quality of road works. Independent National Quality Monitors (NQMs) are also deployed by the Central Government for monitoring the quality of works randomly.

faqs.question: Is There A Provision For The Display Of Project-Related Information At Project Sites?
faqs.answer:
Citizen Information Board in the local language containing the following detailed information of work is provided on each work:-

Description of every layer of work.
Description of the quantity of material involved in work.
How the road will be built and description.
General information board containing information about executing agency, contractor, estimated cost of work and time for completion is also provided on every worksite.

faqs.question: What Is The Role Of Public Representatives In Checking The Quality Of Implementation Of The Programme?
faqs.answer:
In the interest of total transparency and to ensure the pro-active role of public representatives, the States have been advised to organize a time-bound inspection of road works with local public representatives in the following manner:-

The Superintending Engineer would request the Hon'ble M.P. and Zila Pramukh once in 6 months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized.
The Executive Engineer would request the Hon'ble MLA and Chairperson of Intermediate Panchayat once in three months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized.
The Assistant Engineer would request the Sarpanch once in two months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized.

faqs.question: Whether Information About The Programme Is Available On Any Website?
faqs.answer: Yes, information about the programme and details about every work is available on programme website www.omms.nic.in and www.pmgsy.nic.in.The Online Monitoring and Management System (OMMS) is being used for effective management and monitoring under the programme. The required data is entered by the field level staff and the State units under this web-based package.

faqs.question: How Are The Roads Maintained?
faqs.answer: Along with the tendering for the construction the routine maintenance of road works for five years after completion of work is also included. Programme guidelines envisage a transfer of road works for maintenance to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) after 5 years upon completion of the road work.

faqs.question: What Should Be The Population Of Habitations To Be Covered Under PMGSY-I For Providing Connectivity?
faqs.answer: The programme envisages connecting all eligible unconnected habitations by way of an all-weather road as per Core Network with a population of 500 persons (as per 2001 Census) and above in plain areas and 250 persons and above (as per 2001 Census) in the Special Category States (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttarakhand), Tribal (Schedule-V) areas, the Desert Areas (as identified in Desert Development Programme) and in Selected Tribal and Backward Districts (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs/Planning Commission). In the critical 267 Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected blocks (as identified by MHA), additional relaxation has been given to connect habitations with population 100 persons and above (2001 census).

faqs.question: What is the Housing Assistance Scheme?
faqs.answer: It provides housing support to tribal boys and girls pursuing higher education outside their hometown where hostels are not available.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Tribal students from Madhya Pradesh who have passed class 12th and are enrolled in higher education courses.

faqs.question: Does the scheme cover technical and paramedical courses?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme includes technical, paramedical, graduate, and graduate diploma courses.

faqs.question: Can students in private colleges apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, students in non-government colleges are eligible.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available to students who are already staying in government hostels?
faqs.answer: No, the scheme is only for students who have not received admission to government hostels.

faqs.question: What type of financial support is provided?
faqs.answer: Housing assistance is provided to cover accommodation costs for eligible students.

faqs.question: Is there an income limit for eligibility?
faqs.answer: The scheme does not specify an income limit, but applicants must meet other eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: Can students from all districts of Madhya Pradesh apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, students from any district in Madhya Pradesh who meet the criteria can apply.

faqs.question: How do students apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applications can be submitted through the Tribal Welfare and Scheduled Caste (SC) Department of Madhya Pradesh.

faqs.question: Is the scheme available for postgraduate students?
faqs.answer: The scheme is primarily for students pursuing graduate-level courses and specific diplomas. Postgraduate eligibility may depend on the course and department guidelines.

sduk.briefDescription: The scheme "Skill Development" by the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, aims to impart practical training to postgraduate students in various Earth Science disciplines, including structural and evolutionary geology, geochemistry, geomorphology, glaciology, magnetostratigraphy, etc.
sduk.detailedDescription: The scheme "Skill Development" implemented by the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology aims to enhance the practical knowledge and research capabilities of students pursuing Earth Science and allied subjects. Through this scheme, specialised summer and winter training programmes are offered to postgraduate and integrated postgraduate students in disciplines such as geochemistry, sedimentology, tectonics, geomorphology, environmental geoscience, and paleontology.
sduk.benefits: - **Research Experience:** Provides opportunities for self-sponsored research work, allowing students to gain practical experience in Earth Sciences.  - **Seasonal Training:** Offers valuable summer and winter training programs, enhancing practical skills and knowledge in specialized geological disciplines.  - **Exposure to Diverse Fields:** Exposes students to a wide array of sub-disciplines within Earth Sciences, such as structural geology, geochemistry, glaciology, engineering geology, palaeontology, and environmental geology.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: The main objective of the "Skill Development" program is to provide practical training and research exposure to postgraduate students in various branches of Earth sciences to enhance their academic and applied skills.

faqs.question: Who implements the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: The "Skill Development" program is implemented by the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG), under the Government of India.

faqs.question: Which students are eligible to apply for the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: Students who are pursuing postgraduate degrees or are in the fourth or fifth year of integrated postgraduate programs in Earth sciences or related disciplines are eligible to apply for the program.

faqs.question: What types of Earth science disciplines are covered under this program?
faqs.answer: The program covers a wide range of Earth science disciplines including structural geology, geochemistry, sedimentology, geomorphology, tectonics, environmental geology, economic geology, paleontology, and related fields.

faqs.question: Is there a specific degree requirement for eligibility under the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants must be pursuing or should have completed a postgraduate degree in any Earth science, geophysics, geology, or allied field.

faqs.question: What kind of training is provided under the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: The program provides hands-on, field-based and laboratory-based training along with participation in institution-led research activities during the training period.

faqs.question: Does the "Skill Development" program include seasonal training opportunities?
faqs.answer: Yes, the program offers both summer and winter training sessions to accommodate the academic calendars of different institutions.

faqs.question: How can students apply for the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: Students can apply through the official [website ](https://www.wihg.res.in/)of the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology where information regarding the program and application instructions are regularly updated.

faqs.question: Is there a selection process for the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: Yes, the selection process typically involves screening of applications based on academic background, relevance of the research interest, and available seats for the training period.

faqs.question: What are the long-term benefits of attending the "Skill Development" program?
faqs.answer: Participants benefit by acquiring advanced field and laboratory skills, networking with Earth science professionals, and enhancing their academic and research profiles, which helps in future higher education or employment opportunities.

kbocwwb.briefDescription: The "Pension Scheme'' by the BOCW Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Karnataka, is a welfare scheme that aims to provide a monthly pension to registered construction workers who have reached 60 years of age and is a beneficiary of the Board for at least 3 years.

The &quot;Pension Scheme&#39;&#39; by the BOCW Welfare Board, Department of Labour, Karnataka, is a welfare scheme for the registered workers of the board. faqs.question: Who can register as a beneficiary under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of Karnataka?
faqs.answer: Any construction worker whose age is minimum 18 years of age and has worked in any construction work for a minimum of 90 days in a year, are eligible to register as a beneficiary under the Board.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum service requirement to register as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Yes, the building worker must have completed 90 days of service as a building worker in the preceding 12 months.

faqs.question: Who can apply for the welfare scheme?
faqs.answer: Any registered worker of the Board can apply for the welfare scheme.

faqs.question: What are the mandatory documents for the registration?
faqs.answer: The documents required for registration are: Employment Certificate (Form V(A)/V(B)/V(C)/V(D)), Aadhar Card (Self-Attested), Ration Card(non-mandatory), Age Proof (one of them Example: Voter ID Card, Aadhar Card).

faqs.question: How often must a construction worker renew their registration with the Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: A construction worker must renew their registration every 3 years.

faqs.question: What happens if a worker doesn't renew their registration within the 3-year period?
faqs.answer: If a worker doesn't renew their registration within the 3-year period, they are granted a 1-year grace period to complete the renewal.

faqs.question: What happens if a worker doesn't renew their registration during the grace period?
faqs.answer: If the worker fails to renew their registration during the 1-year grace period, their registration will become invalid.

faqs.question: Is there any application fee required for the registration under the Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: No, as per the guidelines, there is no fee required for the registration.

faqs.question: How to enroll as a beneficiary under the Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: Applicants can visit the official Website of Karnataka Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB) to enroll themselves as a beneficiary under the board: https://kbocwwb.karnataka.gov.in/login

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for this pension scheme?
faqs.answer: To be eligible, a worker must be a registered beneficiary of the BOCW Welfare Board, must have completed 60 years of age, must have been a beneficiary of the Board for at least 3 years prior to reaching 60, and must not be receiving similar benefits from other government schemes.

faqs.question: How much pension can a beneficiary receive under this scheme?
faqs.answer: A beneficiary can receive a pension of up to [?]3,000 per month under this scheme.

faqs.question: Can a beneficiary receive this pension if they are already getting a pension from another government scheme?
faqs.answer: No, a beneficiary cannot receive this pension if they are already receiving similar benefits from other government schemes.

faqs.question: What should the legal dependents or heirs do if a pensioner passes away?
faqs.answer: The legal dependents or heirs must inform the BOCW Welfare Board as soon as possible about the death of the pensioner and submit the death certificate to initiate the process of closing the pensioner's bank account.

faqs.question: Why is it important to inform the Board about the death of a pensioner?
faqs.answer: Informing the Board about the death of a pensioner is important to ensure that the pension payments are stopped, and the pensioner's bank account is properly closed, preventing any unauthorized transactions.

faqs.question: What documents are required to notify the Board about the death of a pensioner?
faqs.answer: The legal dependents or heirs need to provide the death certificate of the pensioner to the BOCW Welfare Board.

faqs.question: How to apply for the assistance under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants should visit the official Website of Karnataka Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB) to avail the assistance under this scheme: https://kbocwwb.karnataka.gov.in/login

pi.detailedDescription: Launched by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, the &quot;Pedalandariki Illu&quot; is a Housing Scheme by the Revenue Department, Govt. of Andhra Pradesh. 25 lakh House Site Pattas have been announced for distribution to all the eligible beneficiaries residing in Rural &amp; Urban areas on Saturation Mode irrespective of Caste, Creed, or Religion to facilitate the construction of houses for the homeless poor. The process of issue of House Site Pattas will be taken up on mission mode and distribution to all eligible houseless poor will be taken up. This scheme is also known as the &quot;YSR Housing Scheme&quot; and &quot;YSR Awaas Yojana&quot;.
pi.benefits:

The patta shall be handed over to the beneficiary on the day of Ugadi, 2020. 1. The Housing Department shall issue sanctions for the construction of Individual Housing Units to the eligible beneficiary under the available schemes in a phased manner.
> **Urban Area:** 1. Housing Units shall be constructed following the G+3 pattern at the rate of about 100 units in an extent of Ac.1.00cts. 1. vidya.briefDescription: Vidya scheme under the Education Department, Government of Arunachal Pradesh is a scheme where a girl child who is studying in Class VI is provided with an incentive of Rs. 10,000/- as fixed deposit in SBI in the name of individual girl child till she completes Class – XII.
vidya.detailedDescription:
Vidya scheme under the Education Department, Government of Arunachal Pradesh is a scheme where a girl child who is studying in Class VI is provided with an incentive of ₹10,000/- as fixed deposit in SBI in the name of an individual girl child till she completes Class – XII. After completing Class XII, the Girl child is entitled to receive the maturity amount of the Fixed Deposit. 
**Objective:**

   1. To encourage girl children to continue school education after elementary and secondary levels. 
   1. To encourage the girls to increase their presence in schools and reduce their dropout rate at the elementary and secondary stages of schooling. 
   1. Providing financial assistance/incentive to all female students who successfully pass the Class-V examination and enroll in Class-VI in the State Government Schools. 
   1. The amount of assistance is ₹10,000 from 2015-16 onwards. 
   1. The awarded amount will be deposited in the State Bank of India (SBI) in the name of the girl student as Fixed.
vidya.benefits:

   1. The term/period of deposit may be counted from the date of deposit to the approximate date the girl student passes Class-XII.
   1. No premature withdrawal will be allowed.
   1. Scheme is beneficial one time on successful completion of Class XII.

cmaay.briefDescription: The scheme aims to accord quality and cashless healthcare services to the indigenous people of the state and government employees and reduce out-of-pocket (OOP) expenses during major illness and hospitalization, thereby envisaging universal healthcare for all sections of society.
cmaay.detailedDescription:
Launched on 15th August 2018, "Chief Minister Arogya Arunachal Yojana" is a flagship program of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Arunachal Pradesh. The scheme aims to accord quality and cashless healthcare services to the indigenous people of the state and government employees and reduce out-of-pocket (OOP) expenses during major illness and hospitalization, thereby envisaging universal healthcare for all sections of society.
> **Objectives**


- To reduce the financial hardship on people in the state due to disease and hospitalization.
- To equitably ensure assured access to quality health care for all bonafide citizens of the state.
- To provide quality health care benefits for state government employees and their dependents.
- To make the public health system efficient, effective, and self-reliant by receipt of claim refunds into the individual government hospital accounts. 
- To fulfill the secondary and tertiary health care gap in the state.
cmaay.benefits:
1. Coverage of up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year.
2. Cashless treatments during hospitalization.
3. Pre-existing diseases are inclusively covered.
4. The scheme encompasses expenses for pre-hospitalization for up to 3 days.
5. Post-hospitalization expenses for up to 10 days are covered.
6. Hospitalization expenses include:

- Registration Charges, Bed Charges (General Ward), Nursing and Boarding Charges, Surgeons, Anaesthetists, Medical Practitioners, Consultants Fees, etc..
- Anaesthesia, Blood Transfusion, Oxygen, Operating Theatre (OT) Charges, Cost of Surgical Appliances, etc., Medicines and Drugs, Cost of Prosthetic Devices, Implants, etc., Pathology and Radiology Tests: Radiology to Include but Not Be Limited to X-ray, Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computed Tomography (CT) Scan, etc., Diagnosis and Tests, etc., Food for the Patient.

7. Pre and Post-hospitalization expenses encompass costs incurred for consultation, diagnostic tests, and medicines before the patient's admission to the hospital. Additionally, it covers the cost of diagnostic tests and medicines up to 10 days post-discharge for the same ailment/surgery.
8. All other expenses related to the patient's treatment within the hospital are also covered.
**NOTE:** In the case the applicant has employment with the state government, the insurance program’s benefits are also available to their dependents.
cmaay.exclusions:
> **Conditions That Do Not Require Hospitalization**


- Hospitalization primarily for evaluation / diagnostic purposes
- Any dental treatment or surgery which is corrective, cosmetic or of aesthetic procedure, filling of cavity, root canal including wear and tear etc. unless arising from disease, illness or injury and which requires hospitalization for treatment.
- Congenital external diseases
- Fertility related procedures
- Drugs and Alcohol Induced illness
- Vaccination
- Suicide
- Persistent Vegetative State

faqs.question: How much coverage is provided per family per year for hospitalization and surgical procedures?
faqs.answer: The scheme offers coverage up to [?]5 Lacs per family per year, with [?]1 Lac for secondary ailments and [?]4 Lacs for high-cost tertiary ailments.

faqs.question: Can pre-existing conditions be covered under the Risk Cover?
faqs.answer: Yes, pre-existing conditions/diseases are covered under the Risk Cover, including hospitalization and follow-up care benefits.

faqs.question: What expenses are included in the hospitalization expense benefits package?
faqs.answer: The package covers registration charges, bed charges (General Ward), nursing and boarding charges, surgeons' fees, and other associated costs.

faqs.question: Is there coverage for diagnostic tests like X-ray, MRI, and CT Scan?
faqs.answer: Yes, radiology tests, including X-ray, MRI, CT Scan, etc., are covered under the pathology and radiology tests package.

faqs.question: What is the duration of cashless services for the beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Cashless services are available to the beneficiary from reporting to up to 10 days after discharge from the hospital.

faqs.question: Can medical and surgical packages be taken together for the same patient in the same hospitalization episode?
faqs.answer: No, medical and surgical packages cannot be taken together for the same patient in the same episode of hospitalization.

faqs.question: What is the significance of complications in the context of the procedures?
faqs.answer: Complications are considered a part of the procedure, and they are covered under the policy.

faqs.question: What are the exclusions under the policy regarding hospitalization purposes?
faqs.answer: Conditions not requiring hospitalization, hospitalization primarily for evaluation/diagnostic purposes, and dental treatments for cosmetic or aesthetic procedures are excluded.

faqs.question: Is fertility-related procedures covered under the policy?
faqs.answer: No, fertility-related procedures are excluded from the policy coverage.

faqs.question: Are drugs and alcohol-induced illnesses covered?
faqs.answer: No, illnesses induced by drugs and alcohol are excluded from the policy coverage.

faqs.question: Is there coverage for mental disorders under the medical packages?
faqs.answer: Yes, mental disorders are covered under the Medical Packages, including Emergency Room Packages for care requiring less than 12 hrs stay.

faqs.question: How is the unit of enrollment determined?
faqs.answer: A family is the unit of enrollment, and the head of the family can be either the husband or wife, based on the defined SECC Database.

faqs.question: What is the specific coverage for high-cost tertiary ailments per family per year?
faqs.answer: The coverage for high-cost tertiary ailments is [?]4 Lacs per family per year under the Ayushman Bharat-National Health Protection Mission.

faqs.question: Can beneficiaries claim benefits for pre and post-hospitalization expenses?
faqs.answer: Yes, beneficiaries can claim benefits for pre and post-hospitalization expenses, including consultation, diagnostic tests, and medicines.

faqs.question: How are family units determined for enrollment?
faqs.answer: A family unit for enrollment is based on the SECC Database, and every family in the database is entitled to claim benefits under the mission.

faqs.question: What is the duration covered for pre-hospitalization and post-hospitalization expenses?
faqs.answer: Pre-hospitalization expenses up to 3 days and post-hospitalization expenses up to 10 days are covered for all medicines and diagnostic tests for the same ailment/surgery.

faqs.question: Are there specific specialties covered under the approved list of procedures?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is an approved list of procedures in 23 specialties, including Cardiology, Orthopedics, Urology, and Mental Disorders, among others.

dk.briefDescription: “Dulari Kanya” is a scheme for the girl child by the Govt. of Arunachal Pradesh. The objective of the scheme is to end the preference between male and female child, encouragement of institutional delivery, immunization of children, to end child marriage and overall empowerment of females.
dk.detailedDescription: Announced on 15th August 2016 by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, “Dulari Kanya” is a scheme for the girl child by the Directorate of Family Welfare, Department of Health & Family Welfare of the Govt. of Arunachal Pradesh. The objective of the scheme is to end the preference between male and female child, encouragement of institutional delivery, immunization of children, to end child marriage and overall empowerment of females in all spheres of their life. An amount of ₹ 20,000/- shall be deposited in the fixed deposit Bank Account (Minor Account) of the girl child born in any Government Hospital or Government recognised private hospital. Maturity amount can be withdrawn by the beneficiary on attaining the age of 18 years, which would be subject to verification by the concerned DMO of the respective districts.

aos.briefDescription: Orunodoi, described as 'foremost bead' among the Ashtadash Mukutar Unnoyonee Maala was announced by then HFM in his Budget Speech 20-21. It envisages women empowerment, poverty alleviation and socio-economic inclusion of financially vulnerable women of the state through sustained financial assistanc
aos.benefits:
1) The Assam govt. runs this scheme for those women who belong to the low-income groups of society to support them financially.
2) Each beneficiary will get 1250 rupees per month on the very first date of every month. The Orunodoi 3.0 Scheme covers the expenses for medicines for taking care of health needs, which is 400 rupees per family; Rs. 200 per family is given to provide a 50% subsidy for the 4 kg of pulses of a family; 80 rupees are given as the 50% subsidy for 4 kg of sugar; 150 rupees are given for the fruits & vegetables; Rs. 150 are given for the essential needs; Rs. 170 for covid-19 expenses; and Rs. 250 for a subsidy for 50 units of electricity. And this amount is consolidated to Rs. 1250 per month for a family.
3) Orunodoi Scheme 3.0 will provide financial assistance of Rs. 1250 per month through Direct Benefit Transfer.

Government contractors and suppliers, real estate builders, industrialists, trade license holders who pay income tax. 7. Businessmen/entrepreneurs, Shopkeepers, traders who pay income tax. 8. Land holders other than small and marginal categories. 9. Owning motorized four-wheeler vehicles. 10. Beneficiary under the 'Orunodoi Plus' scheme and any beneficiary of similar scheme, receiving the same cash benefit from State as Orunodoi 3.0, or more than that. 11. ky.briefDescription: In the Krishi Yantra scheme, the farmer purchases farming-related equipment from an authorized dealer, then the state government gives a subsidy to the farmers.
ky.detailedDescription:
The Krishi Yantra Scheme under the Agriculture Department of the Rajasthan government has decided to start the Agricultural Machinery Subsidy Scheme for the convenience of farmers. In this scheme, if the farmer purchases farming equipment from an authorized dealer, then the state government gives a subsidy to the farmers which is 40% of the total price. bsccs.briefDescription: The Bihar Government launched the Bihar Student Credit Card (BSCC) scheme to provide financial aid to applicants to complete their higher education.
bsccs.detailedDescription: The Department of Education introduced a scheme named &quot;**Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme**&quot;. Its aim is to provide financial aid to students to complete their higher education. In this scheme, the students can avail loans of up to ₹4 lakhs at minimal interest rates. They can utilize these funds for financing courses like B.Sc, B.A, B.Tech, or MBBS. This scheme is specifically for all those students who are interested in pursuing higher education but due to lack of financial resources, they are not able to pursue the same.
bsccs.benefits:
The eligible students will get the following benefits under this scheme:-

   1. A maximum loan amount of ₹4 lakh.
   1. Loan can be availed for polytechnic, technical and general courses.
   1. This assistance may be utilized for purchasing of books and laptops or pay any kind of fees.
   1. Repayment of the loan starts once the course has been completed and student have secured a job.
   1. The interest rate of the loan is 1% for Divyang, transgender, and girl students.
   1. The recovery procedures are flexible since the loan is government-owned.

py-jbocwwb.briefDescription: "Pension Yojana (JBOCWWB)" is a scheme by the Department of Labour, Employment, Training & Skill Development Govt of Jharkhand. The scheme provides pension of ₹ 1,000/- per month to those who have contributed to the JBOCWWB for at least 30 years.
py-jbocwwb.detailedDescription: &quot;Pension Yojana (JBOCWWB)&quot; is a scheme by the Department of Labour, Employment, Training &amp; Skill Development Govt of Jharkhand. This is a 100% State Sponsored Scheme. Only the residents/domicile of the state of Jharkhand can apply to this scheme. Applications for this scheme are accepted online through the official website of the department. The scheme provides pension of ₹ 1,000/- per month to those who have contributed to the Jharkhand Building and Other Construction Worker Welfare Board (JBOCWW Board) for at least 30 years.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md:
1. The applicant should be a domicile in the state of Jharkhand.
1. The applicant should have been a Worker registered with the Jharkhand Building and Other Construction Worker Welfare Board (JBOCWW Board).
1. The applicant should be between 18-60 years of age.
1. The applicant should be at least 60 years of age in order to receive the pension.
1. The applicant should have engaged in construction work such as masons, carpenters, electricians, porters, painters, etc.
1. The registered worker should have made continuous contributions for 30 years.

faqs.question: What is the “Mukhyamantri Mahila Udyami Yojana”?
faqs.answer: The "Mukhyamantri Mahila Udyami Yojana" is a component of the "Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana," aimed at promoting entrepreneurship and self-employment among women and transgender individuals in Bihar.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The main objective of the scheme is to empower women and transgender individuals by providing financial assistance to establish and operate business ventures, fostering economic growth and self-reliance.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be a permanent resident of Bihar, be a female or transgender, and be aged between 18 and 50 years.

faqs.question: What educational qualifications are required for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant should have passed at least 10+2, Intermediate, ITI, Polytechnic Diploma, or an equivalent qualification.

faqs.question: What type of businesses are eligible under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The business must be a proprietorship or partnership firm to qualify for assistance under this scheme.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides up to [?]10,00,000/- in financial assistance, with 50% as a non-repayable grant and 50% as an interest-free loan.

faqs.question: Is there any interest charged on the loan component?
faqs.answer: The loan component is interest-free, with a nominal 1% interest charged under specific sub-schemes.

faqs.question: Does the scheme include training programs?
faqs.answer: Yes, mandatory training sessions are provided to enhance the entrepreneurial skills of applicants.

faqs.question: Can transgender individuals apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the scheme is inclusive and provides benefits to transgender individuals along with women.

faqs.question: Is there any age limit for applicants?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants must be between 18 and 50 years of age to qualify for the scheme.

faqs.question: How is the financial assistance disbursed?
faqs.answer: The financial assistance is disbursed in installments, with the first installment released after the completion of mandatory training.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants need to provide proof of residence, educational certificates, identity proof, caste certificate (if applicable), and bank account details, among other required documents.

faqs.question: What happens after the application is approved?
faqs.answer: Once approved, applicants receive the sanctioned amount in their business account. They must utilize the funds as per the project guidelines provided by the department.

faqs.question: What is the Widow Pension Scheme?
faqs.answer: The Widow Pension Scheme is introduced by the Chandigarh Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (CBOCWWB), Labour Department, Chandigarh. The scheme is designed to provide monthly pension support to the widows of male registered construction workers affiliated with the Board.

faqs.question: What financial assistance is provided under the Widow Pension Scheme by the CBOCWWB?
faqs.answer: The Widow Pension Scheme offers financial assistance of [?]1000 per month in the form of a monthly pension to eligible widows of male registered construction workers affiliated with the Board.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria for the Widow Pension Scheme by CBOCWWB?
faqs.answer: To be eligible for the Widow Pension Scheme, the deceased worker should have been employed at an establishment registered under the Punjab Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1965. Additionally, his contribution to the labour welfare fund should have been regularly received by the board.

faqs.question: Are there any exclusions for beneficiaries covered under EPF (Employees' Provident Fund)?
faqs.answer: Yes, financial assistance under the Widow Pension Scheme will not be provided to beneficiaries who are covered under the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF).

faqs.question: How long should the deceased male construction worker have been a member of the Board for the widow to be eligible?
faqs.answer: The widow of a male construction worker is eligible to avail the benefits of the scheme only if the male construction worker was a member of the Board for at least the last six months preceding their demise.

faqs.question: Is there a time limit for widows to apply for the benefits of the scheme?

rgkny.briefDescription: Rajiv Gandhi Kisan Nyay Yojana is a scheme of the Government of Chhattisgarh for the farmers. This scheme was launched on 21 May 2020, on the death anniversary of Rajiv Gandhi.
rgkny.detailedDescription:
Rajiv Gandhi Kisan Nyay Yojana is a scheme of the Government of Chhattisgarh for the farmers and launched on May 21, 2020, on the death anniversary of Rajiv Gandhi.
The main objective of this scheme is to increase the agricultural area by encouraging the farmers for crop production.
Under this scheme, financial benefits will be transferred to the farmers. This amount will be transferred to the accounts of the farmers in 4 instalments. This scheme started during the Corona period has provided great relief to the farmers. In the initial year of the scheme, only paddy, maize and sugarcane crops were included but after that, few more types of following crops have been included in it.

1. Kodo Kutki.
1. Sugarcane.
1. Arhar.
1. Maize.
1. Soybean.
1. Pulses.
1. Oilseeds.
1. Fragrant paddy.
1. Other fortified rice.
1. Banana.
1. Papaya.
rgkny.benefits:
- Maximum amount of 10000/- per acre will be paid to the farmers planting paddy and maize through debit in installments.
- The fixed FRP amount for sugarcane crop will be paid through DBT to farmers at the rate of Rs. 93.75 /- quintal i.e. maximum amount of 355 /- per quintal.

mvy.briefDescription: The scheme aims to eliminate discrimination and inequality against women, improve their health and nutrition, promote economic independence and empowerment, and strengthen their decision-making role in the family.  It offers financial assistance to eligible married women to support their well-being.
mvy.detailedDescription: The scheme "Mahatari Vandan Yojana" by the Government of Chhattisgarh aims to provide financial assistance and support to eligible beneficiaries for socio-economic empowerment. The scheme offers monetary benefits and access to essential services, targeting underserved communities. Key eligibility criteria include residency in Chhattisgarh and possession of an EPIC Card. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Social Welfare, and applications are accepted online through the official portal.
mvy.benefits:
- Each eligible woman will receive ₹1000/- per month.
- Women receiving less than ₹1000/- per month under social assistance programs and various pension schemes through the Samaj Kalyan Vibhag will receive additional assistance to a total ₹1,000/- per month.
- The assistance will be directly deposited into the applicant's Aadhaar-linked DBT-based bank account.
mvy.exclusions:
- The applicant's family must not have any member who is an income taxpayer.    
- The applicant's family must not have any member who is a permanent, temporary, or contractual employee of the Government of India or the State Government in any department/undertaking/board/local body, working in the first, second, or third class position.    
- The applicant's family must not have any member who is a current or former Member of Parliament (MP) or Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA).    
- The applicant's family must not have any member who is a current or former chairman or vice-chairman of any board, corporation, or council of the Government of India or the State Government.

faqs.question: What are the eligibility criteria regarding marital status for applying to this financial assistance scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be a married woman, widow, divorcee, or abandoned woman who is a local resident of Chhattisgarh.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum age requirement to qualify for the monthly financial assistance?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must be 21 years or older as of 1st January of the year of application.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance will an eligible woman receive under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Each eligible beneficiary will receive ₹1,000 per month directly deposited into her Aadhaar-linked bank account.

faqs.question: What happens if a woman already receives some amount under other social assistance programs?
faqs.answer: If she receives less than ₹1,000, she will get additional assistance to make the total ₹1,000 per month.

faqs.question: How will the financial assistance amount be disbursed to the beneficiaries?
faqs.answer: The amount will be transferred directly into the applicant’s Aadhaar-linked DBT-enabled bank account.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to have an Aadhaar-linked bank account to receive the benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant must have her own Aadhaar-linked DBT-based bank account to receive the assistance.

faqs.question: Are there any tax-related exclusions for the applicant’s family under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, no member of the applicant’s family should be an income taxpayer.

faqs.question: Can a woman apply if any family member is employed by the government?
faqs.answer: No, if any family member is a government employee (permanent, temporary, or contractual), she is ineligible.

faqs.question: Are former or current MPs or MLAs or their family members eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, if any family member is or was an MP, MLA, or held certain government positions, the applicant is excluded.

faqs.question: What documents are required to prove local residency in Chhattisgarh?
faqs.answer: Acceptable documents include a residence certificate, ration card, or voter ID card.

faqs.question: Is a marriage certificate mandatory for married women applying to the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, a marriage certificate or a certificate issued by the Gram Panchayat/local bodies is required.

faqs.question: What proof is needed if a woman is abandoned by her husband?
faqs.answer: An abandoned woman must submit a certificate issued by the society/ward/Gram Panchayat as proof.

faqs.question: Which documents can be submitted as proof of age for the applicant?
faqs.answer: Acceptable documents include a birth certificate, 10th/12th marksheet, PAN card, voter ID, or driving license.

faqs.question: Do applicants need to submit a self-declaration or affidavit?
faqs.answer: Yes, a self-declaration form or affidavit must be attached with the application.

hs.briefDescription: A subsidy of Rs. 1,30,000/- is given to persons from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Minority Communities, Single Women, or handicapped for the construction of the house.
hs.detailedDescription: The housing subsidy scheme was launched by the Government of Himachal Pradesh to provide financial assistance to individuals from marginalized sections for the construction of their own houses. Under this scheme, a subsidy of Rs. 1,30,000/- is provided to persons from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Minority Communities, Single Women, or handicapped for the construction of their houses. This scheme aims to improve the living conditions and overall quality of life of individuals from these sections.

eligibilityCriteria.eligibilityDescription_md: 1. The applicant should be a resident of Himachal Pradesh. 2. The applicant should belong to Scheduled Cast, Other Backward Classes, Minority Community, Single Women, or Handicapped. 3. The applicant's annual income should be less than Rs. 3.00 lakhs. 4. The applicant should not have availed of any such subsidy earlier. 5. The applicant should have a bonafide Himachali certificate of the couple. 6. The applicant should possess a Scheduled Cast/Other Backward Classes/Minority Community/Single Women or Handicapped Certificate. 7. The applicant should have income and revenue papers (Record of Right – Parcha & Tatima). 8. The applicant should have a recommendation from the concerned Gram Panchayat. 9. Latest photographs of the present house are required.

faqs.answer: Individuals from Scheduled Cast, Other Backward Classes, Minority Community, Single Women, or handicapped, with an annual income of less than Rs. 3.00 lakhs, and who have not availed any such subsidy earlier, can apply for this scheme.

faqs.question: What Documents Are Required For The Application Process?
faqs.answer: Documents required for the application process include a Bonafide Himachali Certificate of the couple, Scheduled Cast/Other Backward Classes/Minority Community/Single Women or Handicapped Certificate, Income Certificate, Revenue Papers (Record of Right - Parcha & Tatima), Recommendation from the concerned Gram Panchayat, Certificate from the applicant that he/she is not availed any such subsidy earlier, and Latest Photographs of the present house.
